column1: # comment: "Diagnostics-slice alignments to W3C EARL. The match is deliberately loose (skos:closeMatch, not equivalentClass): EARL models an earl:Assertion as a tuple (earl:assertedBy a tool, earl:subject a test subject, earl:result an earl:TestResult with an earl:outcome), whereas a gmeow:Finding is a reified gmeow:Observation (Principle 9) \u2014 the tool is the gmeow:vantage, the offending statement the gmeow:observedFeature, and the severity the gmeow:observationResult \u2014 and is itself one PROJECTION of the canonical Rust report, not a free-standing assertion record. EARL's outcome vocabulary (earl:passed/failed/cantTell) grades the TEST, while gmeow:DiagnosticSeverity grades the FINDING that a test produced, so the alignment of severity to outcome is loose. The internal logic:violation and the native\u2194oracle divergence-ledger entries are restricted Findings in the GMEOW namespace and so are documented in the slice guide rather than mapped here (this file aligns to external vocabularies only)."

column6: earl:Assertion is a tool's (assertedBy, subject, result) tuple; gmeow:Finding is a reified gmeow:Observation about a statement and one projection of the canonical Rust report. closeMatch, not equivalentClass.
earl:outcome grades the TEST (passed/failed/cantTell); gmeow:findingSeverity grades the FINDING a test produced (error/warning/note/info). Related but not the same axis, so a loose closeMatch.
